reviews.fatal_defect: The wave-4 decision rule (K2b threshold kappa and the confirm/kill separation) is derived from a noise model the proposal's own numbers contradict. (i) Phase 0a trains only three block-form configurations on qwen3-0.6b-base (line 559: 3 aggregations x 2 forms x 3 seeds = 18 per base), so the pooled within-configuration seed SD sigma-hat on that base has 6 df, not the "12 df" asserted at lines 453, 575 and 732; kappa = max(0, min(3, 6 - 2*sigma-hat*sqrt(2/5))) is therefore a deterministic function of a variance estimate whose 90% interval spans roughly 0.6x-2x, so the kill threshold can land anywhere from 0 to 3 on estimation noise alone. (ii) The SE used for the five-seed MDE (2*sqrt(2/5) = 1.26, line 739) is seed-only; the manuscript's own paired prompt-level SE of about 1.3 points (line 729) is stated but never combined with it. Combined, se_D is about 1.8 before passage clustering over about 366 sealed passages inflates it further, giving an MDE near 6.2 points rather than 4.3 and a confirm-to-kill separation of about 1.7 SE, not the "at least 2*se_D by construction" claimed. The design is thus still at roughly its own MDE, which is the wave-3 Reviewer A fatal defect surviving in re-derived form. (iii) K1, K2a and sigma-hat are read on the sealed held-out cross-script pairs in Phase 0a (line 573) and Phase 1's primary D is then judged on the same prompts, so the go/no-go gate (a max over 12 configurations x 2 bases) conditions the primary read on the same passage sample, contrary to data.test.identity "untouched by any training or development step".

reviews.verdict: Wave-4 independent reviewer 2: 65/100, under every applicable cap (novelty coverage incomplete and blind discrimination not re-run on the changed mechanism, cap 74; no executable pilot, cap 79; no provider-distinct signed review, cap 89); a falsifier set exists (K1-K6), so the 59 cap does not apply. My scores were fixed before reading the prior scorecard and rise from the authoritative 57 chiefly on controls and identification (5 → 8), where the wave-4 iso-parameter ladder with R_gf as decisive control, the cross-teacher KL sibling with a disagreement precondition, the licensed-target P2/K3 closure and the written per-arm search genuinely resolve the wave-3 defect; the ten-dimension form is otherwise held down by three decision-bearing PARTLY_MEETS criteria (Originality, Methodological Rigor, Evidence Sufficiency) that cannot be compensated by the MEETS on coherence, writing and significance. The fatal blocker is unchanged and known: nothing has executed, the named bundle does not exist, the doctor returns FAIL with acceptedScore 0, and the contract is now stale against the repository (registry commit 53773c3 registers seven of the pilot checkpoints while the YAML still uses stand-ins and says none is registered; retnet, hgrn2 and gsa are still unregistered so Stage C cannot be enabled). The single highest-impact repairable defect is new to this wave: the reported power 0.78 belongs to one leaf of a conjunctive attribution tree, and under the proposal's own noise model the function-induction-class co-condition has power 0.21-0.48 at 3-5 class families, giving a joint CONFIRMED probability of roughly 0.2-0.45 at a true 0.10 effect while a class-level miss is routed to K1 — the kill screen as pre-registered would more often falsely kill a true positive than confirm it. That is fixable on CPU in under an hour by simulating the whole tree and re-tiering a class-level miss into a pre-registered non-kill bucket; until it is fixed, spending the 5.6 GPU-h kill screen would be a poor use of information per GPU-hour. Calibration: NOT_CALIBRATED (single reviewer seat, no empirical target profile; same-provider, unsigned, not provider-distinct).
